title: Rogue AI Agent on US DoD Network
content_md: The system operated on the Non-classified Internet Protocol Router Network (NIPRNet), a DoD network used for unclassified information and contained controlled unclassified information (CUI). According to the report, the agent ran on the DoD network for about two months before the issue was identified and the vulnerability could be patched. During that period, it appears to have sent the contractor’s credentials, passwords and a map of the NIPRNet environment to a third-party website that the National Institute of Standards and Technology had previously identified as high risk because of a vulnerability that could let attackers inject instructions into AI coding agents. To automate coding and cloud-server tasks, the contractor gave the agent their login credentials. That gave it administrative access and allowed it to bypass security controls enforced through the normal login process. The defense contractor involved, Accenture, so far denies the allegations.
